learning: Iteration 10 showed that kd 0.4 drops the score to 175, so kd 0.5 is needed. The best measured controller is kp 3.2 with kd 0.5. Oval steering_oscillation stays near 0.29, a cost accepted for the score.
notes: Final package: the iteration 8 and 9 geometry (score 215.38, reproduced) with the kp 3.2, kd 0.5 controller that produced that score. Kd 0.4 (iteration 10, 174.96) and kp 3.5 (iteration 7, 213.28) were both measured lower, so neither is used.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so the package must be the most reliable design I can justify. The Builder's geometry is the one that raced in iterations 8 and 9 and scored 215.38 both times: wheel_track 0.09 m, five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.024 to +0.024 m and y = 0.04 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.18 m, mass 0.6 kg. I adopt it unchanged. The controller choice needs care. The outcome table shows the kd values by iteration. Iteration 9 (kp 3.2, kd 0.5) scored 215.38, the same as iteration 8, so the result is reproducible. Iteration 7 (kp 3.5, kd 0.5) scored 213.28. Iteration 10 (kp 3.2, kd 0.4) fell to 174.96, so kd 0.5 is needed for the score and kd 0.4 is the wrong direction. The Builder's feedback request cites kp 3.5 as the 215 baseline, which the data does not support: kp 3.5 gave 213.28. The best measured controller is therefore kp 3.2, kd 0.5, ki 0.2, base_speed 1.8, with the iteration 8 and 9 sensor weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2] and line_loss last_direction. Oval steering_oscillation stays near 0.29 at this setting, above the 0.25 caution level, but every kd reduction tested so far lowered the score more than oscillation was worth, so I accept that cost. No further race exists to test an alternative, so the design that has measured best on the development tracks is the safest choice for the unseen track. Expected result: a score near 215 on the development tracks, with the unseen-track result depending on how the held-back track's curvature compares with the oval, s-bend and slalom.
